general_information.Description: Objectives: The goal of this course is to assist students in methodically learning the fundamentals of morphology including morphemes, allomorphs, and morphological processes. The course equips the students with the knowledge and skills to analyze word structures. After the course, students will apply key theoretical frameworks of morphology (such as Lexical Morphology, Distributed Morphology) to analyze linguistic data. They also explore how morphological processes interact with syntax, focusing on word formation and sentence structure. Description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamentals of morphology and its crucial role in the study of linguistics. Students will explore the functions of words, dictionaries, and the mental lexicon in morphological analysis, gaining insight into familiar processes of lexeme formation, such as derivation and compounding, and understanding how new words are created. Furthermore, it addresses the fundamental relationship between morphology and syntax, illustrating how morphological processes can influence phonological forms. Lastly, students will engage with the basic concepts of different morphological theories, enriching their understanding of the field. Teaching and Learning Methodology This course employs an interactive and communicative approach, fostering engaging discussions that enhance understanding of morphology. It incorporates comprehensive guidelines for pre- and post-lesson activities, allowing students to apply and reinforce the skills they have learned. Additionally, the course supports the expansion of knowledge in related fields such as philosophy and applied meaning analysis. A receptive attitude towards questions and potential miscommunications is encouraged, creating an inclusive environment that promotes active learning and collaboration. Finally, linguistic data analysis is used for morphological analysis across specific languages.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible for doing all exercises, assignments, and tasks given by instructors in class or at home and submitting them on time - Use a laptop in class only for learning purposes.
general_information.Tools: Coursebook, Teacher's book, PPTx, handout, Internet

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Categorize various types of morphemes and morphological processes
Explain the relationship between words, dictionaries, and the mental lexicon
Apply familiar lexeme formation processes to new examples
Differentiate between productivity and creativity in morphological processes.
Assess the typological differences in morphological systems across languages and different theories of morphology
Formulate the relationships between morphology, phonology, and syntax
Develop the ability to conduct independent research on morphological topics and present findings clearly and coherently.
Analyze different languages with cultural diversity and awareness of the sociolinguistic factors that influence language use.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Suggested topics: 1.Present word formation rules and Compounding and clarify the contents with specific examples./2. Analyze Productivity versus Creativity. Give examples for each phenomenon/ 3. Demonstrate Internal stem change and provide it with examples./4. Survey sorts of inflection (person, number, gender and noun class, tense and aspect, voice, mood, modality, and evidentiality) that can be found in the languages of the world./ 5. Survey five languages to see what morphological resources they make use of./6. Investigate the relationship between morphology and syntax./7. Describe the intersection between morphology and phonology based on the chapter "Sounds and Shapes: The Interface between Morphology and Phonology". Use specific examples to clarify your ideas./ 8.Discuss the relation between morphology and syntax which can be kept separate from one another.
assessments.Grading Guide: - The purpose of this activity is to assess students' understanding of the concepts and morphological process, the ability to research thoroughly, summarize, and synthesize the knowledge. In addition, students are equipped with presentation, communication, teamwork and active learning skills. Instruction: - The students in class are divided into groups of about 5 students. They choose randomly the topics related to the chapters in the textbook. - Each group will have oral presentation to summarize, analyze and apply the content of an assigned chapter (in 25-30') and demonstrate it by specific instances. - The lecturer will facilitate, consolidate, review, and give comments. Expected Outcomes: - explain examples and process of word formation - comparing morphological phenomena across languages - conducting linguistic research by investigating topics, finding relevant examples - develop the ability to respond to questions from peers and instructors
